notes: Names are full firmware parameter names — never prefix-stripped.
default is null: ArduPilot parameter metadata does not publish defaults. null means unknown, not zero.
type: 'enum'/'bitmask' come from upstream value tables / @Bitmask and are authoritative; 'float' means numeric with storage type not stated.
This is the versioned Copter-4.5 table; the default ardupilot table remains Copter-4.1. Select with --fw-version copter-4.5.

parameters.name: ACRO_BAL_PITCH
parameters.description: rate at which pitch angle returns to level in acro and sport mode. A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster. For helicopter sets the decay rate of the virtual flybar in the pitch axis. A higher value causes faster decay of desired to actual attitude.

parameters.name: ACRO_BAL_ROLL
parameters.description: rate at which roll angle returns to level in acro and sport mode. A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster. For helicopter sets the decay rate of the virtual flybar in the roll axis. A higher value causes faster decay of desired to actual attitude.

parameters.name: ACRO_OPTIONS
parameters.description: A range of options that can be applied to change acro mode behaviour. Air-mode enables ATC_THR_MIX_MAN at all times (air-mode has no effect on helicopters). Rate Loop Only disables the use of angle stabilization and uses angular rate stabilization only.

parameters.name: ACRO_RP_EXPO
parameters.description: Acro roll/pitch Expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

parameters.name: ACRO_RP_RATE
parameters.description: Acro mode maximum roll and pitch rate. Higher values mean faster rate of rotation

parameters.name: ACRO_RP_RATE_TC
parameters.display_name: Acro roll/pitch rate control input time constant
parameters.description: Acro roll and pitch rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

parameters.name: ACRO_THR_MID
parameters.description: Acro Throttle Mid

parameters.name: ACRO_TRAINER
parameters.description: Type of trainer used in acro mode

parameters.name: ACRO_Y_EXPO
parameters.description: Acro yaw expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

parameters.name: ACRO_Y_RATE
parameters.description: Acro mode maximum yaw rate. Higher value means faster rate of rotation

parameters.name: ACRO_Y_RATE_TC
parameters.display_name: Acro yaw rate control input time constant
parameters.description: Acro yaw rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

parameters.name: ADSB_EMIT_TYPE
parameters.description: ADSB classification for the type of vehicle emitting the transponder signal. Default value is 14 (UAV).

parameters.name: ADSB_ICAO_ID
parameters.description: ICAO_ID unique vehicle identification number of this aircraft. This is an integer limited to 24bits. If set to 0 then one will be randomly generated. If set to -1 then static information is not sent, transceiver is assumed pre-programmed.

parameters.name: ADSB_ICAO_SPECL
parameters.description: ICAO_ID of special vehicle that ignores ADSB_LIST_RADIUS and ADSB_LIST_ALT. The vehicle is always tracked. Use 0 to disable.

parameters.name: ADSB_LEN_WIDTH
parameters.description: Aircraft length and width dimension options in Length and Width in meters. In most cases, use a value of 1 for smallest size.

parameters.name: ADSB_LIST_ALT
parameters.description: ADSB vehicle list altitude filter. Vehicles detected above this altitude will be completely ignored. They will not show up in the SRx_ADSB stream to the GCS and will not be considered in any avoidance calculations. A value of 0 will disable this filter.

parameters.name: ADSB_LIST_MAX
parameters.description: ADSB list size of nearest vehicles. Longer lists take longer to refresh with lower SRx_ADSB values.

parameters.name: ADSB_LIST_RADIUS
parameters.description: ADSB vehicle list radius filter. Vehicles detected outside this radius will be completely ignored. They will not show up in the SRx_ADSB stream to the GCS and will not be considered in any avoidance calculations. A value of 0 will disable this filter.

parameters.name: ADSB_LOG
parameters.description: 0: no logging, 1: log only special ID, 2:log all

parameters.name: ADSB_OFFSET_LAT
parameters.description: GPS antenna lateral offset. This describes the physical location offset from center of the GPS antenna on the aircraft.

parameters.name: ADSB_OFFSET_LON
parameters.description: GPS antenna longitudinal offset. This is usually set to 1, Applied By Sensor

parameters.name: ADSB_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Options for emergency failsafe codes and device capabilities

parameters.name: ADSB_RF_CAPABLE
parameters.description: Describes your hardware RF In/Out capabilities.

parameters.name: ADSB_RF_SELECT
parameters.description: Transceiver RF selection for Rx enable and/or Tx enable. This only effects devices that can Tx and/or Rx. Rx-only devices should override this to always be Rx-only.

parameters.name: ADSB_SQUAWK
parameters.description: VFR squawk (Mode 3/A) code is a pre-programmed default code when the pilot is flying VFR and not in contact with ATC. In the USA, the VFR squawk code is octal 1200 (hex 0x280, decimal 640) and in most parts of Europe the VFR squawk code is octal 7000. If an invalid octal number is set then it will be reset to 1200.

parameters.name: ADSB_TYPE
parameters.description: Type of ADS-B hardware for ADSB-in and ADSB-out configuration and operation. If any type is selected then MAVLink based ADSB-in messages will always be enabled

parameters.name: AEROM_ALT_ABORT
parameters.description: Maximum allowable loss in altitude during a trick or sequence from its starting altitude.

parameters.name: AEROM_ANG_ACCEL
parameters.description: Maximum angular acceleration in maneuvers

parameters.name: AEROM_ANG_TC
parameters.description: This is the time over which we filter the desired roll to smooth it

parameters.name: AEROM_BOX_WIDTH
parameters.description: Length of aerobatic "box"

parameters.name: AEROM_DEBUG
parameters.description: This controls the printing of extra debug information on paths

parameters.name: AEROM_ENTRY_RATE
parameters.display_name: The roll rate to use when entering a roll maneuver
parameters.description: This controls how rapidly we roll into a new orientation

parameters.name: AEROM_ERR_COR_D
parameters.display_name: D gain for path error corrections
parameters.description: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path

parameters.name: AEROM_ERR_COR_P
parameters.display_name: P gain for path error corrections
parameters.description: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path

parameters.name: AEROM_KE_RUDD
parameters.description: Percent of rudder normally uses to sustain knife-edge at trick speed

parameters.name: AEROM_KE_RUDD_LK
parameters.description: Time to look ahead in the path to calculate rudder correction for bank angle

parameters.name: AEROM_LKAHD
parameters.description: This is how much time to look ahead in the path for calculating path rates

parameters.name: AEROM_MIS_ANGLE
parameters.description: When set to a non-zero value, this is the assumed direction of the mission. Otherwise the waypoint angle is used

parameters.name: AEROM_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Options to control aerobatic behavior

parameters.name: AEROM_PATH_SCALE
parameters.description: Scale factor for Path/Box size. 0.5 would half the distances in maneuvers. Radii are unaffected.

parameters.name: AEROM_ROL_COR_TC
parameters.description: This is the time constant for correcting roll errors. A smaller value leads to faster roll corrections

parameters.name: AEROM_SPD_I
parameters.description: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error

parameters.name: AEROM_SPD_P
parameters.description: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error

parameters.name: AEROM_STALL_PIT
parameters.description: Pitch threashold for moving to final stage of stall turn

parameters.name: AEROM_STALL_THR
parameters.description: Amount of throttle to reduce to for a stall turn

parameters.name: AEROM_THR_BOOST
parameters.description: This is the extra throttle added in schedule elements marked as needing a throttle boost

parameters.name: AEROM_THR_LKAHD
parameters.description: This controls how far ahead we look in time along the path for the target throttle

parameters.name: AEROM_THR_MIN
parameters.description: Lowest throttle used during maneuvers

parameters.name: AEROM_THR_PIT_FF
parameters.description: This controls how much extra throttle to add based on pitch ange. The value is for 90 degrees and is applied in proportion to pitch

parameters.name: AEROM_TIME_COR_P
parameters.display_name: Time constant for correction of our distance along the path
parameters.description: This is the time constant for correcting path position errors

parameters.name: AEROM_TS_I
parameters.description: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync

parameters.name: AEROM_TS_P
parameters.description: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync

parameters.name: AEROM_TS_RATE
parameters.display_name: Timesync rate of send of NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT data
parameters.description: This sets the rate we send data for time sync between aircraft

parameters.name: AEROM_TS_SPDMAX
parameters.description: This sets the maximum speed adjustment for time sync between aircraft

parameters.name: AEROM_YAW_ACCEL
parameters.description: This is maximum yaw acceleration to use

parameters.name: AFS_AMSL_ERR_GPS
parameters.display_name: Error margin for GPS based AMSL limit
parameters.description: This sets margin for error in GPS derived altitude limit. This error margin is only used if the barometer has failed. If the barometer fails then the GPS will be used to enforce the AMSL_LIMIT, but this margin will be subtracted from the AMSL_LIMIT first, to ensure that even with the given amount of GPS altitude error the pressure altitude is not breached. OBC users should set this to comply with their D2 safety case. A value of -1 will mean that barometer failure will lead to immediate termination.

parameters.name: AFS_AMSL_LIMIT
parameters.description: This sets the AMSL (above mean sea level) altitude limit. If the pressure altitude determined by QNH exceeds this limit then flight termination will be forced. Note that this limit is in meters, whereas pressure altitude limits are often quoted in feet. A value of zero disables the pressure altitude limit.

parameters.name: AFS_DUAL_LOSS
parameters.display_name: Enable dual loss terminate due to failure of both GCS and GPS simultaneously
parameters.description: This enables the dual loss termination part of the AFS system. If this parameter is 1 and both GPS and the ground control station fail simultaneously, this will be considered a "dual loss" and cause termination.

parameters.name: AFS_ENABLE
parameters.description: This enables the advanced failsafe system. If this is set to zero (disable) then all the other AFS options have no effect

parameters.name: AFS_GCS_TIMEOUT
parameters.description: The time (in seconds) of persistent data link loss before GCS failsafe occurs.

parameters.name: AFS_GEOFENCE
parameters.description: This enables the geofence part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

parameters.name: AFS_HB_PIN
parameters.description: This sets a digital output pin which is cycled at 10Hz when termination is not activated. Note that if a FS_TERM_PIN is set then the heartbeat pin will continue to cycle at 10Hz when termination is activated, to allow the termination board to distinguish between autopilot crash and termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: AFS_MAN_PIN
parameters.description: This sets a digital output pin to set high when in manual mode. See the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS
parameters.display_name: Maximum number of comms loss events
parameters.description: Maximum number of comms loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on comms recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of comms loss events.

parameters.name: AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS
parameters.display_name: Maximum number of GPS loss events
parameters.description: Maximum number of GPS loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on GPS recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of GPS loss events.

parameters.name: AFS_MAX_RANGE
parameters.description: This is the maximum range of the vehicle in kilometers from first arming. If the vehicle goes beyond this range then the TERM_ACTION is performed. A value of zero disables this feature.

parameters.name: AFS_OPTIONS
parameters.description: See description for each bitmask bit description

bitmask.0: Continue the mission even after comms are recovered (does not go to the mission item at the time comms were lost)
bitmask.1: Enable AFS for all autonomous modes (not just AUTO)

parameters.name: AFS_QNH_PRESSURE
parameters.description: This sets the QNH pressure in millibars to be used for pressure altitude in the altitude limit. A value of zero disables the altitude limit.

parameters.name: AFS_RC
parameters.description: This enables the RC part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

parameters.name: AFS_RC_FAIL_TIME
parameters.description: This is the time in seconds in manual mode that failsafe termination will activate if RC input is lost. For the OBC rules this should be (1.5). Use 0 to disable.

parameters.name: AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY
parameters.display_name: Enable RC Termination only in manual control modes
parameters.description: If this parameter is set to 1, then an RC loss will only cause the plane to terminate in manual control modes. If it is 0, then the plane will terminate in any flight mode.

parameters.name: AFS_TERMINATE
parameters.description: Can be set in flight to force termination of the heartbeat signal

parameters.name: AFS_TERM_ACTION
parameters.description: This can be used to force an action on flight termination. Normally this is handled by an external failsafe board, but you can setup ArduPilot to handle it here. Please consult the wiki for more information on the possible values of the parameter

parameters.name: AFS_TERM_PIN
parameters.description: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: AFS_WP_COMMS
parameters.description: Waypoint number to navigate to on comms loss

parameters.name: AFS_WP_GPS_LOSS
parameters.description: Waypoint number to navigate to on GPS lock loss

parameters.name: AHRS_COMP_BETA
parameters.display_name: AHRS Velocity Complementary Filter Beta Coefficient
parameters.description: This controls the time constant for the cross-over frequency used to fuse AHRS (airspeed and heading) and GPS data to estimate ground velocity. Time constant is 0.1/beta. A larger time constant will use GPS data less and a small time constant will use air data less.

parameters.name: AHRS_CUSTOM_PIT
parameters.description: Autopilot mounting position pitch offset. Positive values = pitch up, negative values = pitch down. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL
parameters.description: Autopilot mounting position roll offset. Positive values = roll right, negative values = roll left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: AHRS_CUSTOM_YAW
parameters.description: Autopilot mounting position yaw offset. Positive values = yaw right, negative values = yaw left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: AHRS_EKF_TYPE
parameters.display_name: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation
parameters.description: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation

parameters.name: AHRS_GPS_GAIN
parameters.description: This controls how much to use the GPS to correct the attitude. This should never be set to zero for a plane as it would result in the plane losing control in turns. For a plane please use the default value of 1.0.

parameters.name: AHRS_GPS_MINSATS
parameters.description: Minimum number of satellites visible to use GPS for velocity based corrections attitude correction. This defaults to 6, which is about the point at which the velocity numbers from a GPS become too unreliable for accurate correction of the accelerometers.

parameters.name: AHRS_GPS_USE
parameters.display_name: AHRS use GPS for DCM navigation and position-down
parameters.description: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Currently this affects only the DCM-based AHRS: the EKF uses GPS according to its own parameters. A value of 2 means to use GPS for height as well as position - both in DCM estimation and when determining altitude-above-home.

values.2: Use GPS for DCM position and height

parameters.name: AHRS_OPTIONS
parameters.description: This controls optional AHRS behaviour. Setting DisableDCMFallbackFW will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in fly-forward flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DisableDCMFallbackVTOL will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in non fly-forward (VTOL) flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating.

parameters.name: AHRS_ORIENTATION
parameters.description: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for AHRS orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_ROT1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_ROT2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.

parameters.name: AHRS_RP_P
parameters.description: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude

parameters.name: AHRS_TRIM_X
parameters.description: Compensates for the roll angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle roll right.

parameters.name: AHRS_TRIM_Y
parameters.description: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.

parameters.name: AHRS_TRIM_Z
parameters.description: Not Used

parameters.name: AHRS_WIND_MAX
parameters.description: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor by clipping it to groundspeed plus/minus this limit. See ARSPD_OPTIONS and ARSPD_WIND_MAX to disable airspeed sensors.

parameters.name: AHRS_YAW_P
parameters.description: This controls the weight the compass or GPS has on the heading. A higher value means the heading will track the yaw source (GPS or compass) more rapidly.

parameters.name: AIS_LIST_MAX
parameters.description: AIS list size of nearest vessels. Longer lists take longer to refresh with lower SRx_ADSB values.

parameters.name: AIS_LOGGING
parameters.description: Bitmask of AIS logging options

parameters.name: AIS_TIME_OUT
parameters.description: if no updates are received in this time a vessel will be removed from the list

parameters.name: AIS_TYPE
parameters.description: AIS receiver type

parameters.name: ANGLE_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum lean angle in all flight modes

parameters.name: ARMING_ACCTHRESH
parameters.description: Accelerometer error threshold used to determine inconsistent accelerometers. Compares this error range to other accelerometers to detect a hardware or calibration error. Lower value means tighter check and harder to pass arming check. Not all accelerometers are created equal.

parameters.name: ARMING_CHECK
parameters.description: Checks prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks that will be performed before allowing arming. For most users it is recommended to leave this at the default of 1 (all checks enabled). You can select whatever checks you prefer by adding together the values of each check type to set this parameter. For example, to only allow arming when you have GPS lock and no RC failsafe you would set ARMING_CHECK to 72.

parameters.name: ARMING_CRSDP_IGN
parameters.description: Must have value "1" if crashdump data is present on the system, or a prearm failure will be raised. Do not set this parameter unless the risks of doing so are fully understood. The presence of a crash dump means that the firmware currently installed has suffered a critical software failure which resulted in the autopilot immediately rebooting. The crashdump file gives diagnostic information which can help in finding the issue, please contact the ArduPIlot support team. If this crashdump data is present, the vehicle is likely unsafe to fly. Check the ArduPilot documentation for more details.

parameters.name: ARMING_MAGTHRESH
parameters.display_name: Compass magnetic field strength error threshold vs earth magnetic model
parameters.description: Compass magnetic field strength error threshold vs earth magnetic model. X and y axis are compared using this threhold, Z axis uses 2x this threshold. 0 to disable check

parameters.name: ARMING_MIS_ITEMS
parameters.description: Bitmask of mission items that are required to be planned in order to arm the aircraft

parameters.name: ARMING_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Options that can be applied to change arming behaviour

values.2: Do not send status text on state change

parameters.name: ARMING_RUDDER
parameters.description: Allow arm/disarm by rudder input. When enabled arming can be done with right rudder, disarming with left rudder. Rudder arming only works with throttle at zero +- deadzone (RCx_DZ). Depending on vehicle type, arming in certain modes is prevented. See the wiki for each vehicle. Caution is recommended when arming if it is allowed in an auto-throttle mode!

parameters.name: AROT_AS_ACC_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum forward acceleration to apply in speed controller.

parameters.name: AROT_BAIL_TIME
parameters.description: Time in seconds from bail out initiated to the exit of autorotation flight mode.

parameters.name: AROT_COL_FILT_E
parameters.description: Cut-off frequency for collective low pass filter. For the entry phase. Acts as a following trim. Must be higher than AROT_COL_FILT_G.

parameters.name: AROT_COL_FILT_G
parameters.description: Cut-off frequency for collective low pass filter. For the glide phase. Acts as a following trim. Must be lower than AROT_COL_FILT_E.

parameters.name: AROT_ENABLE
parameters.description: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the autonomous autorotation capability.

parameters.name: AROT_FW_V_FF
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. Corrects the target acceleration proportionally to the desired velocity.

parameters.name: AROT_FW_V_P
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) P gain. Determines the proportion of the target acceleration based on the velocity error.

parameters.name: AROT_HS_P
parameters.display_name: P gain for head speed controller
parameters.description: Increase value to increase sensitivity of head speed controller during autonomous autorotation.

parameters.name: AROT_HS_SENSOR
parameters.description: Allocate the RPM sensor instance to use for measuring head speed. RPM1 = 0. RPM2 = 1.

parameters.name: AROT_HS_SET_PT
parameters.description: The target head speed in RPM during autorotation. Start by setting to desired hover speed and tune from there as necessary.

parameters.name: AROT_TARG_SP
parameters.description: Target ground speed in cm/s for the autorotation controller to try and achieve/ maintain during the glide phase.

parameters.name: ARSPD2_AUTOCAL
parameters.display_name: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.
parameters.description: Enables automatic adjustment of airspeed ratio during a calibration flight based on estimation of ground speed and true airspeed. New ratio saved every 2 minutes if change is > 5%. Should not be left enabled.

parameters.name: ARSPD2_BUS
parameters.description: Bus number of the I2C bus where the airspeed sensor is connected. May not correspond to board's I2C bus number labels. Retry another bus and reboot if airspeed sensor fails to initialize.

parameters.name: ARSPD2_DEVID
parameters.description: Airspeed sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

parameters.name: ARSPD2_OFFSET
parameters.description: Airspeed calibration offset

parameters.name: ARSPD2_PIN
parameters.description: The pin number that the airspeed sensor is connected to for analog sensors. Set to 15 on the Pixhawk for the analog airspeed port.

parameters.name: ARSPD2_PSI_RANGE
parameters.display_name: The PSI range of the device
parameters.description: This parameter allows you to set the PSI (pounds per square inch) range for your sensor. You should not change this unless you examine the datasheet for your device

parameters.name: ARSPD2_RATIO
parameters.description: Calibrates pitot tube pressure to velocity. Increasing this value will indicate a higher airspeed at any given dynamic pressure.

parameters.name: ARSPD2_SKIP_CAL
parameters.display_name: Skip airspeed offset calibration on startup
parameters.description: This parameter allows you to skip airspeed offset calibration on startup, instead using the offset from the last calibration. This may be desirable if the offset variance between flights for your sensor is low and you want to avoid having to cover the pitot tube on each boot.

parameters.name: ARSPD2_TUBE_ORDR
parameters.description: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the first (often the top) connector on the sensor needs to be the stagnation pressure (the pressure at the tip of the pitot tube). If set to 1 then the second (often the bottom) connector needs to be the stagnation pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft is receiving excessive pressure on the static port compared to the stagnation port such as during a stall, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed.

parameters.name: ARSPD2_TYPE
parameters.description: Type of airspeed sensor

parameters.name: ARSPD2_USE
parameters.description: This parameter is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

parameters.name: ARSPD_AUTOCAL
parameters.display_name: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.
parameters.description: Enables automatic adjustment of airspeed ratio during a calibration flight based on estimation of ground speed and true airspeed. New ratio saved every 2 minutes if change is > 5%. Should not be left enabled.

parameters.name: ARSPD_DEVID
parameters.description: Airspeed sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

parameters.name: ARSPD_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable airspeed sensor support

parameters.name: ARSPD_OFFSET
parameters.description: Airspeed calibration offset

parameters.name: ARSPD_OFF_PCNT
parameters.description: The maximum percentage speed change in airspeed reports that is allowed due to offset changes between calibrations before a warning is issued. This potential speed error is in percent of ASPD_FBW_MIN. 0 disables. Helps warn of calibrations without pitot being covered.

parameters.name: ARSPD_OPTIONS
parameters.description: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

parameters.name: ARSPD_PIN
parameters.description: The pin number that the airspeed sensor is connected to for analog sensors. Set to 15 on the Pixhawk for the analog airspeed port.

parameters.name: ARSPD_PRIMARY
parameters.description: This selects which airspeed sensor will be the primary if multiple sensors are found

parameters.name: ARSPD_PSI_RANGE
parameters.display_name: The PSI range of the device
parameters.description: This parameter allows you to set the PSI (pounds per square inch) range for your sensor. You should not change this unless you examine the datasheet for your device

This may be desirable if the offset variance between flights for your sensor is low and you want to avoid having to cover the pitot tube on each boot.

The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft is receiving excessive pressure on the static port compared to the stagnation port such as during a stall, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed.

parameters.description: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the first (often the top) connector on the sensor needs to be the stagnation pressure (the pressure at the tip of the pitot tube). If set to 1 then the second (often the bottom) connector needs to be the stagnation pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. parameters.name: ARSPD_TYPE
parameters.description: Type of airspeed sensor

parameters.name: ARSPD_USE
parameters.description: This parameter is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

parameters.name: ARSPD_WIND_GATE
parameters.description: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle.

parameters.name: ARSPD_WIND_MAX
parameters.display_name: Maximum airspeed and ground speed difference
parameters.description: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

parameters.name: ARSPD_WIND_WARN
parameters.display_name: Airspeed and GPS speed difference that gives a warning
parameters.description: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

parameters.name: ATC_ACCEL_P_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum acceleration in pitch axis

parameters.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_SMAX
parameters.description: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

parameters.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MAN
parameters.description: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during manual flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

parameters.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MAX
parameters.description: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during active flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

parameters.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MIN
parameters.description: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used when landing (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_AGGR
parameters.description: Autotune aggressiveness. Defines the bounce back used to detect size of the D term.

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_AXES
parameters.description: 1-byte bitmap of axes to autotune

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_FRQ_MAX
parameters.description: Defines the end frequency for sweeps and dwells

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_FRQ_MIN
parameters.description: Defines the start frequency for sweeps and dwells

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_GN_MAX
parameters.description: Defines the response gain (output/input) to tune

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_MIN_D
parameters.description: Defines the minimum D gain

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_SEQ
parameters.description: 2-byte bitmask to select what tuning should be performed. Max gain automatically performed if Rate D is selected. Values: 7:All,1:VFF Only,2:Rate D/Rate P Only(incl max gain),4:Angle P Only,8:Max Gain Only,16:Tune Check,3:VFF and Rate D/Rate P(incl max gain),5:VFF and Angle P,6:Rate D/Rate P(incl max gain) and angle P

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_VELXY_P
parameters.description: Velocity xy P gain used to hold position during Max Gain, Rate P, and Rate D frequency sweeps

parameters.name: AUTO_OPTIONS
parameters.description: A range of options that can be applied to change auto mode behaviour. Allow Arming allows the copter to be armed in Auto. Allow Takeoff Without Raising Throttle allows takeoff without the pilot having to raise the throttle. Ignore pilot yaw overrides the pilot's yaw stick being used while in auto.

parameters.name: AVD_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable Avoidance using ADSB

parameters.name: AVD_F_ACTION
parameters.description: Specifies aircraft behaviour when a collision is imminent

parameters.name: AVD_F_ALT_MIN
parameters.description: Minimum AMSL (above mean sea level) altitude for ADS-B avoidance. If the vehicle is below this altitude, no avoidance action will take place. Useful to prevent ADS-B avoidance from activating while below the tree line or around structures. Default of 0 is no minimum.

parameters.name: AVD_F_DIST_XY
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before F_ACTION is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_F_DIST_Z
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before BEHAVIOUR_F is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_F_RCVRY
parameters.display_name: Recovery behaviour after a fail event
parameters.description: Determines what the aircraft will do after a fail event is resolved

parameters.name: AVD_F_TIME
parameters.description: Aircraft velocity vectors are multiplied by this time to determine closest approach. If this results in an approach closer than F_DIST_XY or F_DIST_Z then F_ACTION is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_OBS_MAX
parameters.display_name: Maximum number of obstacles to track
parameters.description: Maximum number of obstacles to track

parameters.name: AVD_W_ACTION
parameters.description: Specifies aircraft behaviour when a collision may occur

parameters.name: AVD_W_DIST_XY
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before W_ACTION is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_W_DIST_Z
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before BEHAVIOUR_W is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_W_TIME
parameters.description: Aircraft velocity vectors are multiplied by this time to determine closest approach. If this results in an approach closer than W_DIST_XY or W_DIST_Z then W_ACTION is undertaken (assuming F_ACTION is not undertaken)

parameters.name: AVOID_ACCEL_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum acceleration with which obstacles will be avoided with. Set zero to disable acceleration limits

parameters.name: AVOID_ALT_MIN
parameters.description: Minimum altitude above which proximity based avoidance will start working. This requires a valid downward facing rangefinder reading to work. Set zero to disable

parameters.name: AVOID_ANGLE_MAX
parameters.display_name: Avoidance max lean angle in non-GPS flight modes
parameters.description: Max lean angle used to avoid obstacles while in non-GPS modes

parameters.name: AVOID_BACKUP_DZ
parameters.display_name: Avoidance deadzone between stopping and backing away from obstacle
parameters.description: Distance beyond AVOID_MARGIN parameter, after which vehicle will backaway from obstacles. Increase this parameter if you see vehicle going back and forth in front of obstacle.

parameters.name: AVOID_BACKUP_SPD
parameters.description: Maximum speed that will be used to back away from obstacles horizontally in position control modes (m/s). Set zero to disable horizontal backup.

parameters.name: AVOID_BACKZ_SPD
parameters.description: Maximum speed that will be used to back away from obstacles vertically in height control modes (m/s). Set zero to disable vertical backup.

parameters.name: AVOID_BEHAVE
parameters.description: Avoidance behaviour (slide or stop)

parameters.name: AVOID_DIST_MAX
parameters.display_name: Avoidance distance maximum in non-GPS flight modes
parameters.description: Distance from object at which obstacle avoidance will begin in non-GPS modes

parameters.name: AVOID_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enabled/disable avoidance input sources

parameters.name: AVOID_MARGIN
parameters.display_name: Avoidance distance margin in GPS modes
parameters.description: Vehicle will attempt to stay at least this distance (in meters) from objects while in GPS modes

parameters.description: Barometer sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

parameters.name: BARO1_GND_PRESS
parameters.description: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

parameters.name: BARO1_WCF_BCK
parameters.display_name: Pressure error coefficient in negative X direction (backwards)
parameters.description: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a negative wind relative velocity along the X body axis. If the baro height estimate rises during backwards flight, then this will be a negative number. Multirotors can use this feature only if using EKF3 and if the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters have been tuned.

parameters.name: BARO1_WCF_DN
parameters.display_name: Pressure error coefficient in negative Z direction (down)
parameters.description: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a negative wind relative velocity along the Z body axis. If the baro height estimate rises above truth height during descending flight (or forward flight with a high backwards lean angle, eg braking manoeuvre), then this should be a negative number. Multirotors can use this feature only if using EKF3 and if the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters have been tuned.

parameters.name: BARO_ALTERR_MAX
parameters.description: This is the maximum acceptable altitude discrepancy between GPS altitude and barometric presssure altitude calculated against a standard atmosphere for arming checks to pass. If you are getting an arming error due to this parameter then you may have a faulty or substituted barometer. A common issue is vendors replacing a MS5611 in a "Pixhawk" with a MS5607. If you have that issue then please see BARO_OPTIONS parameter to force the MS5611 to be treated as a MS5607. This check is disabled if the value is zero.

parameters.name: BARO_ALT_OFFSET
parameters.description: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.

parameters.name: BARO_EXT_BUS
parameters.description: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the BARO_PROBE_EXT parameter.

parameters.name: BARO_FIELD_ELV
parameters.description: User provided field elevation in meters. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. Changes to this parameter will only be used when disarmed. A value of 0 means the EKF origin height is used for takeoff height above sea level.

parameters.name: BARO_FLTR_RNG
parameters.display_name: Range in which sample is accepted
parameters.description: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

parameters.name: BARO_GND_TEMP
parameters.description: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.

parameters.name: BARO_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Barometer options

parameters.name: BARO_PRIMARY
parameters.description: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found

parameters.name: BARO_PROBE_EXT
parameters.description: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on BARO_EXT_BUS. If BARO_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in BARO_EXT_BUS.

parameters.name: BATT2_AMP_OFFSET
parameters.description: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor for Analog Sensors. For Synthetic Current sensor, this offset is the zero throttle system current and is added to the calculated throttle base current.

parameters.name: BATT2_AMP_PERVLT
parameters.description: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. With a Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17. For Synthetic Current sensor monitors, this is the maximum, full throttle current draw.

parameters.name: BATT2_ARM_MAH

bitmask.6: Send resistance compensated voltage to GCS
bitmask.7: Allow DroneCAN InfoAux to be from a different CAN node

parameters.name: BATTA_SERIAL_NUM
parameters.description: Battery serial number, automatically filled in for SMBus batteries, otherwise will be -1. With DroneCan it is the battery_id.

parameters.name: BATTA_SHUNT
parameters.description: This sets the shunt resistor used in the device

parameters.name: BATTA_SUM_MASK
parameters.description: 0: sum of remaining battery monitors, If none 0 sum of specified monitors. Current will be summed and voltages averaged.

parameters.name: BATTA_VLT_OFFSET
parameters.description: Voltage offset on voltage pin. This allows for an offset due to a diode. This voltage is subtracted before the scaling is applied.

parameters.name: BATTA_VOLT_MULT
parameters.description: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATTA_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT). For the 3DR Power brick with a Pixhawk, this should be set to 10.1. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 12.02. For the PX using the PX4IO power supply this should be set to 1.

parameters.name: BATTA_VOLT_PIN
parameters.description: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for voltage monitoring.

parameters.name: BATTB_AMP_OFFSET
parameters.description: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor for Analog Sensors. For Synthetic Current sensor, this offset is the zero throttle system current and is added to the calculated throttle base current.

parameters.name: BATTB_AMP_PERVLT
parameters.description: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. With a Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17. For Synthetic Current sensor monitors, this is the maximum, full throttle current draw.

parameters.name: BATTB_ARM_MAH
parameters.description: Battery capacity remaining which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any capacity. Note that execept for smart batteries rebooting the vehicle will always reset the remaining capacity estimate, which can lead to this check not providing sufficent protection, it is recommended to always use this in conjunction with the BATTB__ARM_VOLT parameter.

parameters.name: BATTB_ARM_VOLT
parameters.description: Battery voltage level which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any voltage.

parameters.name: BATTB_CAPACITY
parameters.description: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

parameters.name: BATTB_CRT_MAH
parameters.description: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATTB__FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

parameters.name: BATTB_CRT_VOLT
parameters.description: Battery voltage that triggers a critical battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATTB_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATTB_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

parameters.name: BATTB_CURR_MULT
parameters.description: Multiplier applied to all current related reports to allow for adjustment if no UAVCAN param access or current splitting applications

parameters.name: BATTB_CURR_PIN
parameters.description: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for current monitoring.

parameters.name: BATTB_ESC_INDEX
parameters.display_name: ESC Telemetry Index to write to
parameters.description: ESC Telemetry Index to write voltage, current, consumption and temperature data to. Use 0 to disable.

parameters.name: BATTB_FL_FF
parameters.description: First order polynomial fit term

parameters.name: BATTB_FL_FLTR
parameters.description: Filter frequency in Hertz where a low pass filter is used. This is used to filter out tank slosh from the fuel level reading. parameters.name: BATTB_FL_FS
parameters.description: Second order polynomial fit term

parameters.name: BATTB_FL_FT
parameters.description: Third order polynomial fit term

parameters.name: BATTB_FL_OFF
parameters.description: Offset polynomial fit term

parameters.name: BATTB_FL_PIN

parameters.name: BATTB_FL_VLT_MIN

bitmask.6: Write protect bootloader flash on reboot
bitmask.8: Disable board arming gpio output change on arm/disarm

parameters.name: BRD_PWM_VOLT_SEL
parameters.description: This sets the voltage max for PWM output pulses. 0 for 3.3V and 1 for 5V output. On boards with an IOMCU that support this parameter this option only affects the 8 main outputs, not the 6 auxiliary outputs. Using 5V output can help to reduce the impact of ESC noise interference corrupting signals to the ESCs.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_ABLVL
parameters.description: This sets the minimum RSSI of an auto-bind packet for it to be accepted. This should be set so that auto-bind will only happen at short range to minimise the change of an auto-bind happening accidentially

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_ABTIME
parameters.description: When non-zero this sets the time with no transmitter packets before we start looking for auto-bind packets.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_BZOFS
parameters.description: Set transmitter buzzer note adjustment (adjust frequency up)

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_DEBUG
parameters.description: radio debug level

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_DISCRC
parameters.description: disable receive CRC (for debug)

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_FCCTST
parameters.display_name: Put radio into FCC test mode
parameters.description: If this is enabled then the radio will continuously transmit as required for FCC testing. The transmit channel is set by the value of the parameter. The radio will not work for RC input while this is enabled

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_PPSCH
parameters.description: Channel to show received packet-per-second rate, or zero for disabled

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_PROT
parameters.description: Select air protocol

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_SIGCH
parameters.description: Channel to show receive RSSI signal strength, or zero for disabled

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_STKMD
parameters.description: This selects between different stick input modes. The default is mode2, which has throttle on the left stick and pitch on the right stick. You can instead set mode1, which has throttle on the right stick and pitch on the left stick.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TELEM
parameters.description: If this is non-zero then telemetry packets will be sent over DSM

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TESTCH
parameters.display_name: Set radio to factory test channel
parameters.description: This sets the radio to a fixed test channel for factory testing. Using a fixed channel avoids the need for binding in factory testing.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TPPSCH
parameters.description: Channel to show telemetry packets-per-second value, as received at TX

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TSIGCH
parameters.display_name: RSSI value channel for telemetry data on transmitter
parameters.description: Channel to show telemetry RSSI value as received by TX

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TXMAX
parameters.description: Set transmitter maximum transmit power (from 1 to 8)

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TXPOW
parameters.description: Set telemetry transmit power. This is the power level (from 1 to 8) for telemetry packets sent from the RX to the TX

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TYPE
parameters.display_name: Set type of direct attached radio
parameters.description: This enables support for direct attached radio receivers

parameters.name: BRD_RTC_TYPES
parameters.description: Specifies which sources of UTC time will be accepted

parameters.name: BRD_RTC_TZ_MIN
parameters.description: Adds offset in +- minutes from UTC to calculate local time

parameters.name: BRD_SAFETYOPTION
parameters.description: This controls the activation of the safety button. It allows you to control if the safety button can be used for safety enable and/or disable, and whether the button is only active when disarmed

bitmask.3: Force safety on when the aircraft disarms

parameters.name: BRD_SAFETY_DEFLT
parameters.display_name: Sets default state of the safety switch
parameters.description: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message.

parameters.name: BRD_SAFETY_MASK
parameters.display_name: Outputs which ignore the safety switch state
parameters.description: A bitmask which controls what outputs can move while the safety switch has not been pressed

parameters.name: BRD_SBUS_OUT
parameters.description: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz

parameters.name: BRD_SD_FENCE
parameters.description: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in fence.stg for fence storage.

parameters.name: BRD_SD_MISSION
parameters.description: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in mission.stg for waypoint storage. Each waypoint uses 15 bytes.

parameters.name: BRD_SD_SLOWDOWN
parameters.description: This is a scaling factor to slow down microSD operation. It can be used on flight board and microSD card combinations where full speed is not reliable. For normal full speed operation a value of 0 should be used.

parameters.name: BRD_SER1_RTSCTS
parameters.description: Enable flow control on serial 1 (telemetry 1). You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup. Note that the PX4v1 does not have hardware flow control pins on this port, so you should leave this disabled.

The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup.

parameters.name: BRD_TYPE
parameters.description: This allows selection of a PX4 or VRBRAIN board type. If set to zero then the board type is auto-detected (PX4)

parameters.name: BRD_VBUS_MIN
parameters.description: Minimum voltage on the autopilot power rail to allow the aircraft to arm. 0 to disable the check.

parameters.name: BRD_VSERVO_MIN
parameters.description: Minimum voltage on the servo rail to allow the aircraft to arm. 0 to disable the check.

parameters.name: BTN_ENABLE
parameters.description: This enables the button checking module. When this is disabled the parameters for setting button inputs are not visible

parameters.name: BTN_FUNC1
parameters.description: Auxiliary RC Options function executed on pin change

parameters.name: BTN_FUNC2
parameters.description: Auxiliary RC Options function executed on pin change

parameters.name: BTN_FUNC3
parameters.description: Auxiliary RC Options function executed on pin change

parameters.name: BTN_FUNC4
parameters.description: Auxiliary RC Options function executed on pin change

parameters.name: BTN_OPTIONS1
parameters.description: Options for Pin 1. PWM input detects PWM above or below 1800/1200us instead of logic level. If PWM is not detected or is less than 800us or above 2200us the button will interpreted as low. Invert changes HIGH state to be logic low voltage on pin, or below 1200us, if PWM input.

parameters.name: BTN_OPTIONS2
parameters.description: Options for Pin 2. PWM input detects PWM above or below 1800/1200us instead of logic level. If PWM is not detected or is less than 800us or above 2200us the button will interpreted as low. Invert changes HIGH state to be logic low voltage on pin, or below 1200us, if PWM input.

parameters.description: Options for Pin 3. PWM input detects PWM above or below 1800/1200us instead of logic level. If PWM is not detected or is less than 800us or above 2200us the button will interpreted as low. Invert changes HIGH state to be logic low voltage on pin, or below 1200us, if PWM input.

If PWM is not detected or is less than 800us or above 2200us the button will interpreted as low. Invert changes HIGH state to be logic low voltage on pin, or below 1200us, if PWM input.

parameters.name: BTN_PIN1
parameters.description: Digital pin number for first button input. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: BTN_PIN2
parameters.description: Digital pin number for second button input. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: BTN_PIN3
parameters.description: Digital pin number for third button input. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: BTN_PIN4
parameters.description: Digital pin number for fourth button input. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: BTN_REPORT_SEND
parameters.description: The duration in seconds that a BUTTON_CHANGE report is repeatedly sent to the GCS regarding a button changing state. Note that the BUTTON_CHANGE message is MAVLink2 only.

parameters.name: CAM1_DURATION
parameters.description: Duration in seconds that the camera shutter is held open

parameters.name: CAM1_FEEDBAK_PIN
parameters.description: pin number to use for save accurate camera feedback messages. If set to -1 then don't use a pin flag for this, otherwise this is a pin number which if held high after a picture trigger order, will save camera messages when camera really takes a picture. A universal camera hot shoe is needed. The pin should be held high for at least 2 milliseconds for reliable trigger detection. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot. See also the CAMx_FEEDBCK_POL option.

parameters.name: CAM1_FEEDBAK_POL
parameters.description: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the feedback pin should go high on trigger. If set to 0 then it should go low

parameters.name: CAM1_HFOV
parameters.description: Camera horizontal field of view. 0 if unknown

parameters.name: CAM1_INTRVAL_MIN
parameters.display_name: Camera minimum time interval between photos
parameters.description: Postpone shooting if previous picture was taken less than this many seconds ago

parameters.name: CAM1_MNT_INST
parameters.description: Mount instance camera is associated with. 0 means camera and mount have identical instance numbers e.g. camera1 and mount1

parameters.name: CAM1_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Camera options bitmask

bitmask.0: Recording Starts at arming and stops at disarming

parameters.name: CAM1_RELAY_ON
parameters.description: This sets whether the relay goes high or low when it triggers. Note that you should also set RELAY_DEFAULT appropriately for your camera

parameters.name: CAM1_SERVO_OFF
parameters.description: PWM value in microseconds to move servo to when shutter is deactivated

parameters.name: CAM1_SERVO_ON
parameters.description: PWM value in microseconds to move servo to when shutter is activated

parameters.name: CAM1_TRIGG_DIST
parameters.description: Distance in meters between camera triggers. If this value is non-zero then the camera will trigger whenever the position changes by this number of meters regardless of what mode the APM is in. Note that this parameter can also be set in an auto mission using the DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST command, allowing you to enable/disable the triggering of the camera during the flight.

parameters.name: CAM1_TYPE
parameters.description: how to trigger the camera to take a picture

parameters.name: CAM1_VFOV
parameters.description: Camera vertical field of view. 0 if unknown

parameters.name: CAM_MAX_ROLL
parameters.description: Postpone shooting if roll is greater than limit. (0=Disable, will shoot regardless of roll).

parameters.name: CAM_RC_BTN_DELAY
parameters.display_name: RunCam button delay before allowing further button presses
parameters.description: Time it takes for the a RunCam button press to be actived in ms. If this is too short then commands can get out of sync.

parameters.name: CAM_RC_BT_DELAY
parameters.display_name: RunCam boot delay before allowing updates
parameters.description: Time it takes for the RunCam to become fully ready in ms. If this is too short then commands can get out of sync.

parameters.name: CAM_RC_CONTROL
parameters.description: Specifies the allowed actions required to enter the OSD menu and other option like autorecording

parameters.name: CAM_RC_FEATURES
parameters.description: The available features of the attached RunCam device. If 0 then the RunCam device will be queried for the features it supports, otherwise this setting is used.

parameters.name: CAM_RC_MDE_DELAY
parameters.display_name: RunCam mode delay before allowing further button presses
parameters.description: Time it takes for the a RunCam mode button press to be actived in ms. If a mode change first requires a video recording change then double this value is used. If this is too short then commands can get out of sync.

parameters.name: CAM_RC_TYPE
parameters.description: RunCam device type used to determine OSD menu structure and shutter options.

parameters.description: Custom control type to be used

parameters.display_name: Parachute min altitude in meters above home
parameters.description: Parachute min altitude above home. Parachute will not be released below this altitude. 0 to disable alt check.

parameters.name: CHUTE_CRT_SINK
parameters.display_name: Critical sink speed rate in m/s to trigger emergency parachute
parameters.description: Release parachute when critical sink rate is reached

parameters.name: CHUTE_DELAY_MS
parameters.description: Delay in millseconds between motor stop and chute release

parameters.name: CHUTE_ENABLED
parameters.description: Parachute release enabled or disabled

parameters.name: CHUTE_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Optional behaviour for parachute

parameters.name: CHUTE_SERVO_OFF
parameters.description: Parachute Servo PWM value in microseconds when parachute is not released

parameters.name: CHUTE_SERVO_ON
parameters.description: Parachute Servo PWM value in microseconds when parachute is released

parameters.name: CHUTE_TYPE
parameters.display_name: Parachute release mechanism type (relay or servo)
parameters.description: Parachute release mechanism type (relay number in versions prior to 4.5, or servo). Values 0-3 all are relay. Relay number used for release is set by RELAYx_FUNCTION in 4.5 or later.

parameters.name: CIRCLE_OPTIONS
parameters.description: 0:Enable or disable using the pitch/roll stick control circle mode's radius and rate

bitmask.2: Start at center rather than on perimeter
bitmask.3: Make Mount ROI the center of the circle

parameters.name: CIRCLE_RADIUS
parameters.description: Defines the radius of the circle the vehicle will fly when in Circle flight mode

parameters.name: CIRCLE_RATE
parameters.description: Circle mode's turn rate in deg/sec. Positive to turn clockwise, negative for counter clockwise. Circle rate must be less than ATC_SLEW_YAW parameter.

parameters.name: COMPASS_AUTODEC
parameters.description: Enable or disable the automatic calculation of the declination based on gps location

parameters.name: COMPASS_AUTO_ROT
parameters.description: When enabled this will automatically check the orientation of compasses on successful completion of compass calibration. If set to 2 then external compasses will have their orientation automatically corrected.

values.3: use same tolerance to auto rotate 45 deg rotations

parameters.name: COMPASS_CAL_FIT
parameters.description: This controls the fitness level required for a successful compass calibration. A lower value makes for a stricter fit (less likely to pass). This is the value used for the primary magnetometer. Other magnetometers get double the value.

parameters.name: COMPASS_CUS_PIT
parameters.description: Compass mounting position pitch offset. Positive values = pitch up, negative values = pitch down. This parameter is only used when COMPASS_ORIENT/2/3 is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: COMPASS_CUS_ROLL
parameters.description: Compass mounting position roll offset. Positive values = roll right, negative values = roll left. This parameter is only used when COMPASS_ORIENT/2/3 is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: COMPASS_CUS_YAW
parameters.description: Compass mounting position yaw offset. Positive values = yaw right, negative values = yaw left. This parameter is only used when COMPASS_ORIENT/2/3 is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: COMPASS_DEC

If InFlight learning is enabled then the compass with automatically start learning once a flight starts (must be armed). While InFlight learning is running you cannot use position control modes.

parameters.name: COMPASS_ORIENT
parameters.description: The orientation of the first external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the COMPASS_CUS_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for Compass orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.

The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the COMPASS_CUS_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for Compass orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.
