parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_ATT
parameters.description: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB. Values greater than 40dB will typically produce a hard notch rather than a modest attenuation of motor noise.

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_BW
parameters.description: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz. This is typically set to half the base frequency. The ratio of base frequency to bandwidth determines the notch quality factor and is fixed across harmonics.

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_ENABLE
parameters.description: Harmonic Notch Filter enable

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_FM_RAT
parameters.description: The minimum ratio below the configured frequency to take throttle based notch filters when flying at a throttle level below the reference throttle. Note that lower frequency notch filters will have more phase lag. If you want throttle based notch filtering to be effective at a throttle up to 30% below the configured notch frequency then set this parameter to 0.7. The default of 1.0 means the notch will not go below the frequency in the FREQ parameter.

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_FREQ
parameters.description: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This is the center frequency for static notches, the center frequency for Throttle based notches at the reference thrust value, and the minimum limit of center frequency variation for all other notch types. This should always be set lower than half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz).

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_HMNCS
parameters.description: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of 0 disables this filter. The first harmonic refers to the base frequency.

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_MODE
parameters.display_name: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode
parameters.description: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode. Dynamic updates can be throttle, RPM sensor, ESC telemetry or dynamic FFT based. Throttle-based updates should only be used with multicopters.

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_OPTS
parameters.description: Harmonic Notch Filter options. Triple and double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth with reduced latency than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. Multi-Source attaches a harmonic notch to each detected noise frequency instead of simply being multiples of the base frequency, in the case of FFT it will attach notches to each of three detected noise peaks, in the case of ESC it will attach notches to each of four motor RPM values. Loop rate update changes the notch center frequency at the scheduler loop rate rather than at the default of 200Hz. If both double and triple notches are specified only double notches will take effect.

parameters.name: INS_HNTC2_REF
parameters.description: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value associated with the specified frequency to facilitate frequency scaling of the Harmonic Notch Filter. For RPM and ESC telemetry based tracking, this parameter is set to 1 to enable the Harmonic Notch Filter using the RPM sensor or ESC telemetry set to measure rotor speed. The sensor data is converted to Hz automatically for use in the Harmonic Notch Filter. This reference value may also be used to scale the sensor data, if required. For example, rpm sensor data is required to measure heli motor RPM. Therefore the reference value can be used to scale the RPM sensor to the rotor RPM.

If the IMU cannot be moved and velocity noise is a problem, a location closer to the IMU can be used as the body frame origin.

parameters.name: INS_POS3_Z

Attention: The IMU should be located as close to the vehicle c.g. as practical so that the value of this parameter is minimised. Failure to do so can result in noisy navigation velocity measurements due to vibration and IMU gyro noise. parameters.name: LOG_BACKEND_TYPE
parameters.description: Bitmap of what Logger backend types to enable. Block-based logging is available on SITL and boards with dataflash chips. Multiple backends can be selected.

parameters.name: LOG_BITMASK
parameters.description: Bitmap of what on-board log types to enable. This value is made up of the sum of each of the log types you want to be saved. It is usually best just to enable all basiclog types by setting this to 65535.

parameters.name: LOG_BLK_RATEMAX
parameters.display_name: Maximum logging rate for block backend
parameters.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the block backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

parameters.name: LOG_DARM_RATEMAX
parameters.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to any backend when disarmed. A value of zero means that the normal backend rate limit is applied.

parameters.name: LOG_DISARMED
parameters.description: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled at all times including when disarmed. Logging before arming can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues and is necessary if logging of EKF replay data is selected via the LOG_REPLAY parameter. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 2, then logging will be enabled when disarmed, but not if a USB connection is detected. This can be used to prevent unwanted data logs being generated when the vehicle is connected via USB for log downloading or parameter changes. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 3 then logging will happen while disarmed, but if the vehicle never arms then the logs using the filesystem backend will be discarded on the next boot.

values.3: Discard log on reboot if never armed

parameters.name: LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE
parameters.display_name: Maximum AP_Logger File and Block Backend buffer size (in kilobytes)
parameters.description: The File and Block backends use a buffer to store data before writing to the block device. Raising this value may reduce "gaps" in your SD card logging. This buffer size may be reduced depending on available memory. PixHawk requires at least 4 kilobytes. Maximum value available here is 64 kilobytes.

parameters.name: LOG_FILE_DSRMROT
parameters.display_name: Stop logging to current file on disarm
parameters.description: When set, the current log file is closed when the vehicle is disarmed. If LOG_DISARMED is set then a fresh log will be opened. Applies to the File and Block logging backends.

parameters.name: LOG_FILE_MB_FREE
parameters.display_name: Old logs on the SD card will be deleted to maintain this amount of free space
parameters.description: Set this such that the free space is larger than your largest typical flight log

parameters.name: LOG_FILE_RATEMAX
parameters.display_name: Maximum logging rate for file backend
parameters.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the file backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

parameters.name: LOG_FILE_TIMEOUT
parameters.display_name: Timeout before giving up on file writes
parameters.description: This controls the amount of time before failing writes to a log file cause the file to be closed and logging stopped.

parameters.name: LOG_MAV_BUFSIZE
parameters.display_name: Maximum AP_Logger MAVLink Backend buffer size
parameters.description: Maximum amount of memory to allocate to AP_Logger-over-mavlink

parameters.name: LOG_MAV_RATEMAX
parameters.display_name: Maximum logging rate for mavlink backend
parameters.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the mavlink backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

parameters.name: LOG_MAX_FILES
parameters.description: This sets the maximum number of log file that will be written on dataflash or sd card before starting to rotate log number. Limit is capped at 500 logs.

parameters.name: LOG_REPLAY
parameters.display_name: Enable logging of information needed for Replay
parameters.description: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 and EKF3 state estimators will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. LOG_DISARMED must be set to 1 or 2 or else the log will not contain the pre-flight data required for replay testing of the EKF's. It is suggested that you also raise LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE to give more buffer space for logging and use a high quality microSD card to ensure no sensor data is lost.

parameters.name: NTF_LED_LEN
parameters.description: The number of Serial LED's to use for notifications (NeoPixel's and ProfiLED)

parameters.name: NTF_LED_OVERRIDE
parameters.display_name: Specifies colour source for the RGBLed
parameters.description: Specifies the source for the colours and brightness for the LED. OutbackChallenge conforms to the MedicalExpress (https://uavchallenge.org/medical-express/) rules, essentially "Green" is disarmed (safe-to-approach), "Red" is armed (not safe-to-approach). Traffic light is a simplified color set, red when armed, yellow when the safety switch is not surpressing outputs (but disarmed), and green when outputs are surpressed and disarmed, the LED will blink faster if disarmed and failing arming checks.

parameters.name: NTF_LED_TYPES
parameters.description: Controls what types of LEDs will be enabled

parameters.name: NTF_OREO_THEME

parameters.name: OA_BR_CONT_RATIO

parameters.description: BendyRuler will avoid changing bearing unless ratio of previous margin from obstacle (or fence) to present calculated margin is atleast this much.

parameters.name: OA_BR_LOOKAHEAD
parameters.display_name: Object Avoidance look ahead distance maximum
parameters.description: Object Avoidance will look this many meters ahead of vehicle

parameters.name: OA_BR_TYPE
parameters.description: BendyRuler will search for clear path along the direction defined by this parameter

parameters.name: OA_DB_ALT_MIN
parameters.display_name: OADatabase minimum altitude above home before storing obstacles
parameters.description: OADatabase will reject obstacles if vehicle's altitude above home is below this parameter, in a 3 meter radius around home. Set 0 to disable this feature.

parameters.name: OA_DB_BEAM_WIDTH
parameters.description: Beam width of incoming lidar data

parameters.name: OA_DB_DIST_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum distance of objects held in database. Set to zero to disable the limits

parameters.name: OA_DB_EXPIRE
parameters.description: OADatabase item timeout. The time an item will linger without any updates before it expires. Zero means never expires which is useful for a sent-once static environment but terrible for dynamic ones.

parameters.name: OA_DB_OUTPUT
parameters.description: OADatabase output level to configure which database objects are sent to the ground station. All data is always available internally for avoidance algorithms.

values.2: Send HIGH and NORMAL importance items

parameters.name: OA_DB_QUEUE_SIZE
parameters.display_name: OADatabase queue maximum number of points
parameters.description: OADatabase queue maximum number of points. This in an input buffer size. Larger means it can handle larger bursts of incoming data points to filter into the database. No impact on cpu, only RAM. Recommend larger for faster datalinks or for sensors that generate a lot of data.

parameters.name: OA_DB_RADIUS_MIN
parameters.description: Minimum radius of objects held in database

parameters.name: OA_DB_SIZE
parameters.description: OADatabase maximum number of points. Set to 0 to disable the OA Database. Larger means more points but is more cpu intensive to process

parameters.name: OA_MARGIN_MAX
parameters.description: Object Avoidance will ignore objects more than this many meters from vehicle

parameters.name: OA_OPTIONS
parameters.display_name: Options while recovering from Object Avoidance
parameters.description: Bitmask which will govern vehicles behaviour while recovering from Obstacle Avoidance (i.e Avoidance is turned off after the path ahead is clear).

parameters.description: Enabled/disable path planning around obstacles

parameters.name: OSD_ARM_SCR
parameters.description: Screen to be shown on Arm event. Zero to disable the feature.

parameters.name: OSD_BTN_DELAY
parameters.description: Debounce time in ms for stick commanded parameter navigation.

parameters.name: OSD_CELL_COUNT
parameters.description: Used for average cell voltage display. -1 disables, 0 uses cell count autodetection for well charged LIPO/LIION batteries at connection, other values manually select cell count used.

parameters.name: OSD_CHAN
parameters.description: This sets the channel used to switch different OSD screens.

parameters.name: OSD_DSARM_SCR
parameters.description: Screen to be shown on disarm event. Zero to disable the feature.

parameters.name: OSD_FONT
parameters.description: This sets which OSD font to use. It is an integer from 0 to the number of fonts available

parameters.name: OSD_FS_SCR
parameters.description: Screen to be shown on failsafe event. Zero to disable the feature.

parameters.name: OSD_H_OFFSET
parameters.description: Sets horizontal offset of the osd inside image

parameters.name: OSD_MSG_TIME
parameters.description: Sets message duration seconds

parameters.name: OSD_OPTIONS
parameters.description: This sets options that change the display

bitmask.3: Convert feet to miles at 5280ft instead of 10000ft

parameters.name: OSD_SW_METHOD
parameters.description: This sets the method used to switch different OSD screens.

values.0: switch to next screen if channel value was changed
values.1: select screen based on pwm ranges specified for each screen
values.2: switch to next screen after low to high transition and every 1s while channel value is high

parameters.name: OSD_TYPE
parameters.description: OSD type. TXONLY makes the OSD parameter selection available to other modules even if there is no native OSD support on the board, for instance CRSF.

parameters.name: OSD_TYPE2
parameters.description: OSD type 2. TXONLY makes the OSD parameter selection available to other modules even if there is no native OSD support on the board, for instance CRSF.

parameters.name: OSD_UNITS
parameters.description: Sets the units to use in displaying items

parameters.name: OSD_V_OFFSET
parameters.description: Sets vertical offset of the osd inside image

parameters.name: OSD_W_ACRVOLT
parameters.display_name: Avg Cell Resting Volt warn level
parameters.description: Set level at which ACRVOLT item will flash

parameters.name: OSD_W_AVGCELLV
parameters.description: Set level at which AVGCELLV item will flash

parameters.name: OSD_W_BATVOLT
parameters.description: Set level at which BAT_VOLT item will flash

parameters.name: OSD_W_LQ
parameters.description: Set level at which RC_LQ item will flash (%)

parameters.name: OSD_W_NSAT
parameters.description: Set level at which NSAT item will flash

parameters.name: OSD_W_RESTVOLT
parameters.description: Set level at which RESTVOLT item will flash

parameters.name: OSD_W_RSSI
parameters.description: Set level at which RSSI item will flash (in positive % or negative dBm values as applicable). 30% or -100dBm are defaults.

parameters.name: OSD_W_SNR
parameters.description: Set level at which RC_SNR item will flash (in db)

parameters.name: OSD_W_TERR
parameters.description: Set level below which TER_HGT item will flash. -1 disables.

parameters.name: PHLD_BRAKE_ANGLE
parameters.description: PosHold flight mode's max lean angle during braking in centi-degrees

parameters.name: PHLD_BRAKE_RATE
parameters.description: PosHold flight mode's rotation rate during braking in deg/sec

parameters.name: PILOT_ACCEL_Z
parameters.description: The vertical acceleration used when pilot is controlling the altitude

parameters.name: PILOT_SPEED_DN
parameters.description: The maximum vertical descending velocity the pilot may request in cm/s. If 0 PILOT_SPEED_UP value is used.

parameters.name: PILOT_SPEED_UP
parameters.description: The maximum vertical ascending velocity the pilot may request in cm/s

parameters.name: PILOT_THR_BHV
parameters.description: Bitmask containing various throttle stick options. TX with sprung throttle can set PILOT_THR_BHV to "1" so motor feedback when landed starts from mid-stick instead of bottom of stick.

parameters.name: PILOT_THR_FILT
parameters.description: Throttle filter cutoff (Hz) - active whenever altitude control is inactive - 0 to disable

parameters.name: PILOT_TKOFF_ALT
parameters.description: Altitude that altitude control modes will climb to when a takeoff is triggered with the throttle stick.

parameters.name: PILOT_Y_EXPO
parameters.description: Pilot controlled yaw expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

parameters.name: PILOT_Y_RATE
parameters.description: Pilot controlled yaw rate max. Used in all pilot controlled modes except Acro

parameters.name: PILOT_Y_RATE_TC
parameters.display_name: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant
parameters.description: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

parameters.name: PLDP_DELAY
parameters.description: Delay after release, in seconds, before aircraft starts to climb back to starting altitude.

parameters.name: PLDP_RNG_MIN
parameters.display_name: Payload Place minimum range finder altitude
parameters.description: Minimum range finder altitude in m to trigger payload touchdown, set to zero to disable.

parameters.name: PLDP_SPEED_DN
parameters.description: The maximum vertical decent velocity in m/s. If 0 LAND_SPEED value is used.

parameters.name: PLDP_THRESH
parameters.description: Ratio of vertical thrust during decent below which payload touchdown will trigger.

parameters.name: PLND_ACC_P_NSE
parameters.description: Kalman Filter Accelerometer Noise, higher values weight the input from the camera more, accels less

parameters.name: PLND_ALT_CUTOFF
parameters.description: The altitude (rangefinder distance) below which we stop using the precision landing sensor and continue landing

parameters.name: PLND_ALT_MAX
parameters.description: Vehicle will continue landing vertically until this height if target is not found. Below this height if landing target is not found, landing retry/failsafe might be attempted. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zero to disable this.

parameters.name: PLND_ALT_MIN
parameters.description: Vehicle will continue landing vertically even if target is lost below this height. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zero to disable this.

parameters.name: PLND_BUS
parameters.description: Precland sensor bus for I2C sensors.

parameters.name: PLND_CAM_POS_X
parameters.description: X position of the camera in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin.

parameters.name: PLND_CAM_POS_Y
parameters.description: Y position of the camera in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin.

parameters.name: PLND_CAM_POS_Z
parameters.description: Z position of the camera in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin.

parameters.name: PLND_ENABLED
parameters.description: Precision Land enabled/disabled

parameters.name: PLND_EST_TYPE
parameters.description: Specifies the estimation method to be used

parameters.name: PLND_LAG
parameters.description: Precision Landing sensor lag, to cope with variable landing_target latency

parameters.name: PLND_LAND_OFS_X
parameters.description: Desired landing position of the camera forward of the target in vehicle body frame

parameters.name: PLND_LAND_OFS_Y
parameters.description: desired landing position of the camera right of the target in vehicle body frame

parameters.name: PLND_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Precision Landing Extra Options

bitmask.1: Allow Precision Landing after manual reposition
bitmask.2: Maintain high speed in final descent

parameters.name: PLND_ORIENT
parameters.description: Orientation of camera/sensor on body

parameters.name: PLND_RET_BEHAVE
parameters.description: Prec Land will do the action selected by this parameter if a retry to a landing is needed

values.0: Go to the last location where landing target was detected
values.1: Go towards the approximate location of the detected landing target

parameters.name: PLND_RET_MAX
parameters.display_name: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing
parameters.description: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing. Set to zero to disable landing retry.

parameters.name: PLND_STRICT
parameters.description: How strictly should the vehicle land on the target if target is lost

parameters.name: PLND_TIMEOUT
parameters.description: Time for which vehicle continues descend even if target is lost. After this time period, vehicle will attempt a landing retry depending on PLND_STRICT parameter.

parameters.name: PLND_TYPE
parameters.description: Precision Land Type

parameters.name: PLND_XY_DIST_MAX
parameters.display_name: Precision Landing maximum distance to target before descending
parameters.description: The vehicle will not start descending if the landing target is detected and it is further than this many meters away. Set 0 to always descend.

parameters.name: PLND_YAW_ALIGN
parameters.description: Yaw angle from body x-axis to sensor x-axis.

parameters.name: POI_DIST_MAX
parameters.description: POI's max distance (in meters) from the vehicle

parameters.name: PREV_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable parameter reversion system

parameters.name: PREV_RC_FUNC
parameters.description: RCn_OPTION number to used to trigger parameter reversion

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_D
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired vertical acceleration vs actual acceleration

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_D_FF
parameters.description: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_FF
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller feed forward

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_FLTD
parameters.display_name: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_FLTE
parameters.display_name: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_FLTT
parameters.display_name: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_I
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_IMAX
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm that the I term will generate

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_NEF
parameters.description: Accel (vertical) Error notch filter index

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_NTF
parameters.description: Accel (vertical) Target notch filter index

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_P
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration into a motor output

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_PDMX
parameters.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

parameters.name: PSC_ACCZ_SMAX
parameters.description: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

parameters.name: PSC_ACC_XY_FILT
parameters.description: Lower values will slow the response of the navigation controller and reduce twitchiness

parameters.name: PSC_ANGLE_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum lean angle autopilot can request. Set to zero to use ANGLE_MAX parameter value

parameters.name: PSC_JERK_XY
parameters.display_name: Jerk limit for the horizontal kinematic input shaping
parameters.description: Jerk limit of the horizontal kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

parameters.name: PSC_JERK_Z
parameters.display_name: Jerk limit for the vertical kinematic input shaping
parameters.description: Jerk limit of the vertical kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

parameters.name: PSC_POSXY_P
parameters.description: Position controller P gain. Converts the distance (in the latitude direction) to the target location into a desired speed which is then passed to the loiter latitude rate controller

parameters.name: PSC_POSZ_P
parameters.description: Position (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between the desired altitude and actual altitude into a climb or descent rate which is passed to the throttle rate controller

parameters.name: PSC_VELXY_D
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity

parameters.name: PSC_VELXY_FF
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) feed forward gain. Converts the difference between desired velocity to a target acceleration

parameters.name: PSC_VELXY_FLTD
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D term

parameters.name: PSC_VELXY_FLTE
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms

parameters.name: PSC_VELXY_I
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) I gain. Corrects long-term difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration

parameters.name: PSC_VELXY_IMAX
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) integrator maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output

parameters.name: PSC_VELXY_P
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) P gain. Converts the difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration

parameters.name: PSC_VELZ_D
parameters.description: Velocity (vertical) controller D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity

parameters.name: PSC_VELZ_FF
parameters.description: Velocity (vertical) controller Feed Forward gain. Produces an output that is proportional to the magnitude of the target

parameters.name: PSC_VELZ_FLTD
parameters.display_name: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term
parameters.description: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D terms

parameters.name: PSC_VELZ_FLTE
parameters.description: Velocity (vertical) error filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms

parameters.name: PSC_VELZ_I
parameters.description: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired velocity to a target acceleration

parameters.name: PSC_VELZ_IMAX
parameters.description: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output

parameters.name: PSC_VELZ_P
parameters.description: Velocity (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller

parameters.name: QUIK_AUTO_FILTER
parameters.description: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER

parameters.name: QUIK_AUTO_SAVE
parameters.description: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune

parameters.name: QUIK_AXES
parameters.description: axes to tune

parameters.name: QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME
parameters.description: Time to double a tuning parameter. Raise this for a slower tune.

parameters.name: QUIK_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable quicktune system

parameters.name: QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN
parameters.description: Reduction in gain after oscillation detected. Raise this number to get a more conservative tune

parameters.name: QUIK_MAX_REDUCE
parameters.description: This controls how much quicktune is allowed to lower gains from the original gains. If the vehicle already has a reasonable tune and is not oscillating then you can set this to zero to prevent gain reductions. The default of 20% is reasonable for most vehicles. Using a maximum gain reduction lowers the chance of an angle P oscillation happening if quicktune gets a false positive oscillation at a low gain, which can result in very low rate gains and a dangerous angle P oscillation.

parameters.name: QUIK_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Additional options. When the Two Position Switch option is enabled then a high switch position will start the tune, low will disable the tune. you should also set a QUIK_AUTO_SAVE time so that you will be able to save the tune.

parameters.name: QUIK_OSC_SMAX
parameters.description: Threshold for oscillation detection. A lower value will lead to a more conservative tune.

parameters.name: QUIK_RC_FUNC
parameters.description: RCn_OPTION number to use to control tuning stop/start/save

parameters.name: QUIK_RP_PI_RATIO
parameters.description: Ratio between P and I gains for roll and pitch. Raise this to get a lower I gain

parameters.name: QUIK_YAW_D_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum value for yaw D gain

parameters.name: QUIK_YAW_P_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum value for yaw P gain

parameters.name: QUIK_Y_PI_RATIO
parameters.description: Ratio between P and I gains for yaw. Raise this to get a lower I gain

parameters.name: RALLY_INCL_HOME
parameters.description: Controls if Home is included as a Rally point (i.e. as a safe landing place) for RTL

parameters.name: RALLY_LIMIT_KM
parameters.description: Maximum distance to rally point. If the closest rally point is more than this number of kilometers from the current position and the home location is closer than any of the rally points from the current position then do RTL to home rather than to the closest rally point. This prevents a leftover rally point from a different airfield being used accidentally. If this is set to 0 then the closest rally point is always used.

parameters.name: RALLY_TOTAL
parameters.description: Number of rally points currently loaded

parameters.name: RCK_DEBUG
parameters.description: Sends Rockblock debug text to GCS via statustexts

parameters.name: RCK_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enables the Rockblock sending and recieving

parameters.name: RCK_FORCEHL
parameters.description: Automatically enables High Latency mode if not already enabled

parameters.name: RCK_PERIOD
parameters.description: When in High Latency mode, send Rockblock updates every N seconds

parameters.name: RCMAP_PITCH
parameters.description: Pitch channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Pitch is normally on channel 2, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

parameters.name: RCMAP_ROLL
parameters.description: Roll channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Roll is normally on channel 1, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

parameters.name: RCMAP_THROTTLE
parameters.description: Throttle channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Throttle is normally on channel 3, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

parameters.name: RCMAP_YAW
parameters.description: Yaw channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Yaw (also known as rudder) is normally on channel 4, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

parameters.name: RC_FS_TIMEOUT
parameters.description: RC failsafe will trigger this many seconds after loss of RC

parameters.name: RC_OPTIONS
parameters.description: RC input options

bitmask.2: Ignore Receiver Failsafe bit but allow other RC failsafes if setup
bitmask.6: Skip the arming check for neutral Roll/Pitch/Yaw sticks
bitmask.9: Suppress CRSF mode/rate message for ELRS systems
bitmask.11: Use Link Quality for RSSI with CRSF
bitmask.12: Annotate CRSF flight mode with * on disarm

parameters.name: RC_OVERRIDE_TIME
parameters.description: Timeout after which RC overrides will no longer be used, and RC input will resume, 0 will disable RC overrides, -1 will never timeout, and continue using overrides until they are disabled

parameters.name: RC_PROTOCOLS
parameters.description: Bitmask of enabled RC protocols. Allows narrowing the protocol detection to only specific types of RC receivers which can avoid issues with incorrect detection. Set to 1 to enable all protocols.

parameters.name: RC_SPEED
parameters.description: This is the speed in Hertz that your ESCs will receive updates

parameters.name: RCn_DZ
parameters.description: PWM dead zone in microseconds around trim or bottom

parameters.name: RCn_MAX
parameters.description: RC maximum PWM pulse width in microseconds. Typically 1000 is lower limit, 1500 is neutral and 2000 is upper limit.

parameters.name: RCn_MIN
parameters.description: RC minimum PWM pulse width in microseconds. Typically 1000 is lower limit, 1500 is neutral and 2000 is upper limit.

parameters.name: RCn_OPTION
parameters.description: Function assigned to this RC channel

parameters.name: RCn_REVERSED
parameters.description: Reverse channel input. Set to 0 for normal operation. Set to 1 to reverse this input channel.

parameters.name: RCn_TRIM
parameters.description: RC trim (neutral) PWM pulse width in microseconds. Typically 1000 is lower limit, 1500 is neutral and 2000 is upper limit.

parameters.display_name: Distance (in cm) from the range finder to the ground
parameters.description: This parameter sets the expected range measurement(in cm) that the range finder should return when the vehicle is on the ground.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_MAX_CM
parameters.description: Maximum distance in centimeters that rangefinder can reliably read

parameters.name: RNGFND1_MIN_CM
parameters.description: Minimum distance in centimeters that rangefinder can reliably read

parameters.name: RNGFND1_OFFSET
parameters.description: Offset in volts for zero distance for analog rangefinders. Offset added to distance in centimeters for PWM lidars

parameters.name: RNGFND1_ORIENT
parameters.description: Orientation of rangefinder

parameters.name: RNGFND1_PIN
parameters.description: Analog or PWM input pin that rangefinder is connected to. Airspeed ports can be used for Analog input, AUXOUT can be used for PWM input. parameters.name: RNGFND1_POS_X
parameters.description: X position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_POS_Y
parameters.description: Y position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_POS_Z
parameters.description: Z position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_PWRRNG
parameters.description: This parameter sets the estimated terrain distance in meters above which the sensor will be put into a power saving mode (if available). A value of zero means power saving is not enabled

parameters.name: RNGFND1_RECV_ID
parameters.description: The receive ID of the CAN frames. A value of zero means all IDs are accepted.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_RMETRIC
parameters.description: This parameter sets whether an analog rangefinder is ratiometric. Most analog rangefinders are ratiometric, meaning that their output voltage is influenced by the supply voltage. Some analog rangefinders (such as the SF/02) have their own internal voltage regulators so they are not ratiometric.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_SCALING
parameters.description: Scaling factor between rangefinder reading and distance. For the linear and inverted functions this is in meters per volt. For the hyperbolic function the units are meterVolts. For Maxbotix serial sonar this is unit conversion to meters.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_SNR_MIN
parameters.description: RangeFinder Minimum signal strength (SNR) to accept distance

parameters.name: RNGFND1_STOP_PIN
parameters.description: Digital pin that enables/disables rangefinder measurement for the pwm rangefinder. A value of -1 means no pin. If this is set, then the pin is set to 1 to enable the rangefinder and set to 0 to disable it. This is used to enable powersaving when out of range. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_TYPE
parameters.description: Type of connected rangefinder

parameters.name: RNGFND1_WSP_AVG
parameters.description: Sets the number of pulses to be used in multi-pulse averaging mode. In this mode, a sequence of rapid fire ranges are taken and then averaged to improve the accuracy of the measurement

parameters.name: RNGFND1_WSP_BAUD
parameters.description: Desired baud rate

parameters.name: RNGFND1_WSP_FRQ
parameters.description: Sets the repetition frequency of the ranging operation in Hertz. Upon entering the desired frequency the system will calculate the nearest frequency that it can handle according to the resolution of internal timers.

parameters.name: RNGFND1_WSP_MAVG
parameters.description: Sets the number of historic range results to use for calculating the current range result. When MAVG is greater than 1, the current range result will be the current measured value averaged with the N-1 previous results

parameters.name: RNGFND1_WSP_MEDF
parameters.description: Sets the window size for the real-time median filter. When MEDF is greater than 0 the median filter is active

parameters.name: RNGFND1_WSP_THR
parameters.description: Sets the system sensitivity. Larger values of THR represent higher sensitivity. The system may limit the maximum value of THR to prevent excessive false alarm rates based on settings made at the factory. Set to -1 for automatic threshold adjustments

parameters.name: RNGFND6_STOP_PIN
parameters.description: Digital pin that enables/disables rangefinder measurement for the pwm rangefinder. A value of -1 means no pin. If this is set, then the pin is set to 1 to enable the rangefinder and set to 0 to disable it. This is used to enable powersaving when out of range. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

parameters.name: RNGFND6_TYPE
parameters.description: Type of connected rangefinder

parameters.name: RNGFND6_WSP_AVG
parameters.description: Sets the number of pulses to be used in multi-pulse averaging mode. In this mode, a sequence of rapid fire ranges are taken and then averaged to improve the accuracy of the measurement

parameters.name: RNGFND6_WSP_BAUD
parameters.description: Desired baud rate

parameters.name: RNGFND6_WSP_FRQ
parameters.description: Sets the repetition frequency of the ranging operation in Hertz. Upon entering the desired frequency the system will calculate the nearest frequency that it can handle according to the resolution of internal timers.

parameters.name: RNGFND6_WSP_MAVG
parameters.description: Sets the number of historic range results to use for calculating the current range result. When MAVG is greater than 1, the current range result will be the current measured value averaged with the N-1 previous results

parameters.name: RNGFND6_WSP_MEDF
parameters.description: Sets the window size for the real-time median filter. When MEDF is greater than 0 the median filter is active

parameters.name: RNGFND6_WSP_THR
parameters.description: Sets the system sensitivity. Larger values of THR represent higher sensitivity. The system may limit the maximum value of THR to prevent excessive false alarm rates based on settings made at the factory. Set to -1 for automatic threshold adjustments

parameters.name: RNGFND7_ADDR
parameters.description: This sets the bus address of the sensor, where applicable. Used for the I2C and DroneCAN sensors to allow for multiple sensors on different addresses.

parameters.name: RNGFND7_FUNCTION
parameters.description: Control over what function is used to calculate distance. For a linear function, the distance is (voltage-offset)*scaling. For a inverted function the distance is (offset-voltage)*scaling. For a hyperbolic function the distance is scaling/(voltage-offset). The functions return the distance in meters.

parameters.name: RNGFND7_GNDCLEAR
parameters.display_name: Distance (in cm) from the range finder to the ground
parameters.description: This parameter sets the expected range measurement(in cm) that the range finder should return when the vehicle is on the ground.

parameters.name: RNGFND7_MAX_CM

parameters.name: RNGFND7_MIN_CM

parameters.name: RNGFND7_OFFSET
parameters.description: Offset in volts for zero distance for analog rangefinders. Offset added to distance in centimeters for PWM lidars

parameters.name: RNGFND7_ORIENT
parameters.description: Orientation of rangefinder

parameters.name: RNGFND7_PIN
parameters.description: Analog or PWM input pin that rangefinder is connected to. Airspeed ports can be used for Analog input, AUXOUT can be used for PWM input. parameters.name: RSSI_ANA_PIN
parameters.description: Pin used to read the RSSI voltage or PWM value

parameters.name: RSSI_CHANNEL
parameters.description: The channel number where RSSI will be output by the radio receiver (5 and above).

parameters.name: RSSI_CHAN_HIGH
parameters.description: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_CHAN_LOW

parameters.name: RSSI_CHAN_LOW
parameters.description: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_CHAN_HIGH

parameters.name: RSSI_PIN_HIGH
parameters.description: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_PIN_LOW. When using pin 103, the maximum value of the parameter is 3.3V.

parameters.name: RSSI_PIN_LOW
parameters.description: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_PIN_HIGH. When using pin 103, the maximum value of the parameter is 3.3V.

parameters.name: RSSI_TYPE
parameters.description: Radio Receiver RSSI type. If your radio receiver supports RSSI of some kind, set it here, then set its associated RSSI_XXXXX parameters, if any.

parameters.name: RTL_ALT
parameters.description: The minimum alt above home the vehicle will climb to before returning. If the vehicle is flying higher than this value it will return at its current altitude.

parameters.name: RTL_ALT_FINAL
parameters.description: This is the altitude the vehicle will move to as the final stage of Returning to Launch or after completing a mission. Set to zero to land.

parameters.name: RTL_ALT_TYPE
parameters.description: RTL altitude type. Set to 1 for Terrain following during RTL and then set WPNAV_RFND_USE=1 to use rangefinder or WPNAV_RFND_USE=0 to use Terrain database

parameters.name: RTL_CLIMB_MIN
parameters.description: The vehicle will climb this many cm during the initial climb portion of the RTL

parameters.name: RTL_CONE_SLOPE
parameters.description: Defines a cone above home which determines maximum climb

parameters.name: RTL_LOIT_TIME
parameters.description: Time (in milliseconds) to loiter above home before beginning final descent

parameters.name: RTL_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Options that can be applied to change RTL mode behaviour

parameters.name: RTL_SPEED
parameters.description: Defines the speed in cm/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain horizontally while flying home. If this is set to zero, WPNAV_SPEED will be used instead.

parameters.name: RTUN_AUTO_FILTER
parameters.description: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER

parameters.name: RTUN_AUTO_SAVE
parameters.description: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune

parameters.name: RTUN_AXES
parameters.description: axes to tune

parameters.name: RTUN_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable quicktune system

parameters.name: RTUN_RC_FUNC
parameters.description: RCn_OPTION number to use to control tuning stop/start/save

parameters.name: RTUN_SPD_FFRATIO
parameters.description: Ratio between measured response and CRUISE_THROTTLE value. Raise this to get a higher CRUISE_THROTTLE value

parameters.name: RTUN_SPD_I_RATIO
parameters.display_name: Rover Quicktune Speed FF to I ratio
parameters.description: Ratio between speed FF and I gain. Raise this to get a higher I gain, 0 to leave I unchanged

parameters.name: RTUN_SPD_P_RATIO
parameters.display_name: Rover Quicktune Speed FF to P ratio
parameters.description: Ratio between speed FF and P gain. Raise this to get a higher P gain, 0 to leave P unchanged

parameters.name: RTUN_STR_FFRATIO
parameters.display_name: Rover Quicktune Steering Rate FeedForward ratio
parameters.description: Ratio between measured response and FF gain. Raise this to get a higher FF gain

parameters.name: RTUN_STR_I_RATIO
parameters.display_name: Rover Quicktune Steering FF to I ratio
parameters.description: Ratio between steering FF and I gains. Raise this to get a higher I gain, 0 to leave I unchanged

parameters.name: RTUN_STR_P_RATIO
parameters.display_name: Rover Quicktune Steering FF to P ratio
parameters.description: Ratio between steering FF and P gains. Raise this to get a higher P gain, 0 to leave P unchanged

parameters.name: SCHED_DEBUG
parameters.description: Set to non-zero to enable scheduler debug messages. When set to show "Slips" the scheduler will display a message whenever a scheduled task is delayed due to too much CPU load. When set to ShowOverruns the scheduled will display a message whenever a task takes longer than the limit promised in the task table.

parameters.name: SCHED_LOOP_RATE
parameters.description: This controls the rate of the main control loop in Hz. This should only be changed by developers. This only takes effect on restart. Values over 400 are considered highly experimental.

parameters.name: SCHED_OPTIONS
parameters.description: This controls optional aspects of the scheduler.

parameters.name: SCR_DEBUG_OPTS
parameters.description: Debugging options

bitmask.0: No Scripts to run message if all scripts have stopped
bitmask.1: Runtime messages for memory usage and execution time
bitmask.3: log runtime memory usage and execution time
bitmask.5: Save CRC of current scripts to loaded and running checksum parameters enabling pre-arm

parameters.name: SCR_DIR_DISABLE
parameters.description: This will stop scripts being loaded from the given locations

parameters.name: SCR_ENABLE
parameters.description: Controls if scripting is enabled

parameters.name: SCR_HEAP_SIZE
parameters.description: Amount of memory available for scripting

parameters.name: SCR_LD_CHECKSUM
parameters.description: Required XOR of CRC32 checksum of loaded scripts, vehicle will not arm with incorrect scripts loaded, -1 disables

parameters.name: SCR_RUN_CHECKSUM
parameters.description: Required XOR of CRC32 checksum of running scripts, vehicle will not arm with incorrect scripts running, -1 disables

parameters.name: SCR_THD_PRIORITY
parameters.description: This sets the priority of the scripting thread. This is normally set to a low priority to prevent scripts from interfering with other parts of the system. Advanced users can change this priority if scripting needs to be prioritised for realtime applications. WARNING: changing this parameter can impact the stability of your flight controller. The scipting thread priority in this parameter is chosen based on a set of system level priorities for other subsystems. It is strongly recommended that you use the lowest priority that is sufficient for your application. Note that all scripts run at the same priority, so if you raise this priority you must carefully audit all lua scripts for behaviour that does not interfere with the operation of the system.

parameters.name: SERIAL_PASS1
parameters.description: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port

parameters.name: SERIAL_PASS2
parameters.description: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port

parameters.name: SERIAL_PASSTIMO
parameters.description: This sets a timeout for serial pass-through in seconds. When the pass-through is enabled by setting the SERIAL_PASS1 and SERIAL_PASS2 parameters then it remains in effect until no data comes from the first port for SERIAL_PASSTIMO seconds. This allows the port to revent to its normal usage (such as MAVLink connection to a GCS) when it is no longer needed. A value of 0 means no timeout.

parameters.name: SERVO_32_ENABLE
parameters.description: This allows for up to 32 outputs, enabling parameters for outputs above 16

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_3DMASK
parameters.description: Mask of channels which are dynamically reversible. This is used to configure ESCs in '3D' mode, allowing for the motor to spin in either direction

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_AUTO
parameters.display_name: BLHeli pass-thru auto-enable for multicopter motors
parameters.description: If set to 1 this auto-enables BLHeli pass-thru support for all multicopter motors

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_BDMASK
parameters.display_name: BLHeli bitmask of bi-directional dshot channels
parameters.description: Mask of channels which support bi-directional dshot. This is used for ESCs which have firmware that supports bi-directional dshot allowing fast rpm telemetry values to be returned for the harmonic notch.

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_DEBUG
parameters.description: When set to 1 this enabled verbose debugging output over MAVLink when the blheli protocol is active. This can be used to diagnose failures.

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_MASK
parameters.description: Enable of BLHeli pass-thru servo protocol support to specific channels. This mask is in addition to motors enabled using SERVO_BLH_AUTO (if any)

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_OTYPE
parameters.description: When set to a non-zero value this overrides the output type for the output channels given by SERVO_BLH_MASK. This can be used to enable DShot on outputs that are not part of the multicopter motors group.

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_POLES
parameters.description: This allows calculation of true RPM from ESC's eRPM. The default is 14.

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_PORT
parameters.description: This sets the mavlink channel to use for blheli pass-thru. The channel number is determined by the number of serial ports configured to use mavlink. So 0 is always the console, 1 is the next serial port using mavlink, 2 the next after that and so on.

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_RVMASK
parameters.description: Mask of channels which are reversed. This is used to configure ESCs in reversed mode

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_TEST
parameters.description: Setting SERVO_BLH_TEST to a motor number enables an internal test of the BLHeli ESC protocol to the corresponding ESC. The debug output is displayed on the USB console.

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_TMOUT
parameters.description: This sets the inactivity timeout for the BLHeli protocol in seconds. If no packets are received in this time normal MAVLink operations are resumed. A value of 0 means no timeout

parameters.name: SERVO_BLH_TRATE
parameters.description: This sets the rate in Hz for requesting telemetry from ESCs. It is the rate per ESC. Setting to zero disables telemetry requests

parameters.name: SERVO_DSHOT_ESC
parameters.description: DShot ESC type for all outputs. The ESC type affects the range of DShot commands available and the bit widths used. None means that no dshot commands will be executed. Some ESC types support Extended DShot Telemetry (EDT) which allows telemetry other than RPM data to be returned when using bi-directional dshot. If you enable EDT you must install EDT capable firmware for correct operation.

parameters.name: SERVO_DSHOT_RATE
parameters.description: DShot output rate for all outputs as a multiple of the loop rate. 0 sets the output rate to be fixed at 1Khz for low loop rates. This value should never be set below 500Hz.

parameters.name: SERVO_FTW_MASK
parameters.description: Servo channel mask specifying FETtec ESC output.

parameters.name: SERVO_FTW_POLES
parameters.description: Number of motor electrical poles

parameters.name: SERVO_FTW_RVMASK
parameters.description: Servo channel mask to reverse rotation of FETtec ESC outputs.

parameters.name: SERVO_GPIO_MASK
parameters.description: Bitmask of outputs which will be available as GPIOs. Any output with either the function set to -1 or with the corresponding bit set in this mask will be available for use as a GPIO pin

parameters.name: SERVO_RATE
parameters.description: Default output rate in Hz for all PWM outputs.

parameters.name: SERVO_RC_FS_MSK
parameters.description: Bitmask of scaled passthru output channels which will be set to their trim value during rc failsafe instead of holding their last position before failsafe.

parameters.name: SERVO_ROB_POSMAX
parameters.description: Position maximum at servo max value. This should be within the position control range of the servos, normally 0 to 4095

parameters.name: SERVO_ROB_POSMIN
parameters.description: Position minimum at servo min value. This should be within the position control range of the servos, normally 0 to 4095

parameters.name: SERVO_SBUS_RATE

parameters.name: SERVO_VOLZ_MASK
parameters.description: Enable of volz servo protocol to specific channels

parameters.name: SERVOn_FUNCTION
parameters.description: Function assigned to this servo. Setting this to Disabled(0) will setup this output for control by auto missions or MAVLink servo set commands. any other value will enable the corresponding function

parameters.name: SERVOn_MAX
parameters.description: maximum PWM pulse width in microseconds. Typically 1000 is lower limit, 1500 is neutral and 2000 is upper limit.

parameters.name: SERVOn_MIN
parameters.description: minimum PWM pulse width in microseconds. Typically 1000 is lower limit, 1500 is neutral and 2000 is upper limit.

parameters.name: SERVOn_REVERSED
parameters.description: Reverse servo operation. Set to 0 for normal operation. Set to 1 to reverse this output channel.

parameters.name: SERVOn_TRIM
parameters.description: Trim PWM pulse width in microseconds. Typically 1000 is lower limit, 1500 is neutral and 2000 is upper limit.

parameters.name: SHIP_AUTO_OFS
parameters.description: Settings this parameter to one triggers an automatic follow offset calculation based on current position of the vehicle and the landing target. NOTE: This parameter will auto-reset to zero once the offset has been calculated.

parameters.name: SHIP_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable ship landing system

parameters.name: SHIP_LAND_ANGLE
parameters.description: Angle from the stern of the ship for landing approach. Use this to ensure that on a go-around that ship superstructure and cables are avoided. A value of zero means to approach from the rear of the ship. A value of 90 means the landing will approach from the port (left) side of the ship. A value of -90 will mean approaching from the starboard (right) side of the ship. A value of 180 will approach from the bow of the ship. This parameter is combined with the sign of the RTL_RADIUS parameter to determine the holdoff pattern. If RTL_RADIUS is positive then a clockwise loiter is performed, if RTL_RADIUS is negative then a counter-clockwise loiter is used.

parameters.name: TERRAIN_ENABLE
parameters.description: enable terrain data. This enables the vehicle storing a database of terrain data on the SD card. The terrain data is requested from the ground station as needed, and stored for later use on the SD card. To be useful the ground station must support TERRAIN_REQUEST messages and have access to a terrain database, such as the SRTM database.

parameters.name: TERRAIN_MARGIN
parameters.description: Margin in centi-meters to accept terrain data from the GCS. This can be used to allow older terrain data generated with less accurate latitude/longitude scaling to be used

parameters.name: TERRAIN_OFS_MAX
parameters.description: The maximum adjustment of terrain altitude based on the assumption that the vehicle is on the ground when it is armed. When the vehicle is armed the location of the vehicle is recorded, and when terrain data is available for that location a height adjustment for terrain data is calculated that aligns the terrain height at that location with the altitude recorded at arming. This height adjustment is applied to all terrain data. This parameter clamps the amount of adjustment. A value of zero disables the use of terrain height adjustment.

parameters.name: TERRAIN_OPTIONS
parameters.description: Options to change behaviour of terrain system

parameters.name: TERRAIN_SPACING
parameters.description: Distance between terrain grid points in meters. This controls the horizontal resolution of the terrain data that is stored on te SD card and requested from the ground station. If your GCS is using the ArduPilot SRTM database like Mission Planner or MAVProxy, then a resolution of 100 meters is appropriate. Grid spacings lower than 100 meters waste SD card space if the GCS cannot provide that resolution. The grid spacing also controls how much data is kept in memory during flight. A larger grid spacing will allow for a larger amount of data in memory. A grid spacing of 100 meters results in the vehicle keeping 12 grid squares in memory with each grid square having a size of 2.7 kilometers by 3.2 kilometers. Any additional grid squares are stored on the SD once they are fetched from the GCS and will be loaded as needed.

parameters.name: THROW_TYPE

parameters.name: THR_DZ
